title: DIY Holographic Display
tagline: A persistence-of-vision LED cylinder that renders 3D holographic-like visuals in mid-air.
problem: I wanted to explore volumetric displays — the kind that make light appear to float in 3D space. Commercial options cost thousands. Could I build something similar from scratch for under ₹2000?

components.name: ESP32 Dev Board
components.purpose: Main controller + Wi-Fi for frame upload

components.name: WS2812B LED Strip
components.purpose: 60 LEDs/m, 30cm length = 18 addressable LEDs per arm

components.name: Hall Effect Sensor
components.purpose: RPM sync — detects one full rotation

components.name: Neodymium Magnet
components.purpose: Triggers Hall sensor once per revolution

components.name: DC Brushless Motor
components.purpose: Spinning the LED arm at ~600 RPM

components.name: Slip Ring (6-wire)
components.purpose: Power + data transfer to spinning assembly

components.name: 3D Printed Frame
components.purpose: LED arm mount and motor coupling

components.name: 5V 3A Power Supply
components.purpose: LED strip power (draws up to 2A at full white)

results.status: Prototype — text and simple shapes render clearly, complex images need improvement
